Ensure every merge gateway inside the cycle has a path to an end event. On the passing outcome, flow directly onward. On the failing outcome, place a task that performs the corrective action (obtaining the difference). Connect that task's outgoing flow, and the passing outcome's flow, into one exclusive merge gateway placed before the next step, so that the corrective task's flow joins at the merge. Do not leave the failing outcome without its corrective task, and do not connect the corrective task directly to the next step without the merge.

When the description says a check or review of an earlier work product ends in one of two outcomes, and each outcome is followed either by a further described action or by termination of the process: Model the check as a task in the lane of the party that performs it, and model the recording of its outcome as a separate task in that same lane. Place an exclusive gateway after the outcome task, with one branch per outcome. On each branch, model the described follow-up action as its own task, including any return to an earlier actor for repetition and any continuation to the next stage. Where the description gives no follow-up action for an outcome, route that branch directly to an end event named for that outcome. Do not merge the two outcomes, do not place the follow-up action before the gateway, and do not replace a described action with a bare sequence flow or an end event that carries the action's meaning.

When The description says that the team may optionally perform one or more activities before a later step (for example with 'may also', 'optionally' or 'if needed'), and the activities are not required on every path.: Place an exclusive gateway before the optional activities. One outgoing flow performs the optional activities, and another flow bypasses them. Reconverge the paths at an exclusive gateway merge before the next step. Do not use a parallel gateway for the merge, and do not make the optional activities mandatory in sequence.
